headline: Eight days to the crossing and the taper is fully engaged. Legs are banked, strength held to the last, and the quiet is deliberate. The audit begins when the trail does.
confidence_reasons: Limited data sources active in last 3 days

sections.overview: The picture this week is coherent taper, not a stall. Running has gone quiet by design after the block's build-up peaked, and today's cardio-load ratio reading of zero simply reflects a genuinely runless recent stretch — it flags "detraining" mechanically, but the demonstrated engine underneath is intact and rested, not eroded. Strength has done the more interesting thing: rather than dropping to zero into the pre-travel window, it's held a steady cadence of short functional sessions, keeping the system live without adding fatigue. Steps remain high on active days, which matters more than usual right now — it keeps the legs warm into departure — though the rest-day zeros are the one place the picture goes fully cold. Sleep is unremarkable as context and shouldn't shift anything. This is a body being deliberately under-loaded ahead of a long sustained effort, and every piece points the same way.
sections.trends: The 16-week shape shows a real build peaking a couple of weeks back, then the intentional draw-down you'd expect this close to a 580 km effort — that's a clean taper arc, not an irregular one. Year-to-date, the contrast with last year is stark: this season's accumulated volume is more than quadruple the same point in 2025, which is the base that makes the current quiet affordable. The monthly progression makes sense against a hybrid athlete who isn't strictly periodising but has clearly leaned into a specific event window here. The shape is doing what it should.
sections.threshold: Threshold pace and the bpm it sits at are unchanged from the 30-day baseline — flat, and flat is exactly right during a taper. There's no new stimulus expected to move it and none should be sought now. What matters is that the number hasn't drifted the wrong way despite the reduced running load, which is consistent with fitness being banked rather than bleeding. VO2/threshold work is not the job this week; holding what's there is.
sections.zones: The recent per-session shapes tell the taper story better than any weekly aggregate. The final harder session before the quiet was a genuine mixed tempo effort with real time up in the higher zones — a proper fast stimulus — and everything since has sat comfortably in the easy aerobic range, with the most recent run almost entirely Z1/Z2 and only a token touch higher. That's the correct sequence: sharpen once, then keep it conversational. No grey-zone creep in the easy runs, which is what you want when the goal is freshness rather than fitness gain.
sections.hr_comparison: The strength sessions continue to sit low and controlled in the aerobic range, which fits their functional-maintenance role rather than anything taxing — appropriate for this window. Nothing in the source agreement between the run and strength HR streams stands out as inconsistent; the estimates track sensibly with effort and duration. No concern here.
sections.calendar: Beyond the raw streak, the texture worth noting is that strength has quietly become the connective tissue holding the week together while running went dark — sessions spaced every couple of days, never long, never absent. That's a deliberate way to stay athletically "on" through a running taper without accumulating fatigue. The one gap in the pattern remains the fully cold rest days on the step side, which is the only place consistency breaks cleanly to zero.
sections.personal_bests: No PBs are in play this week and none should be — the training intent right now is durability and freshness for a multi-day effort, which is the opposite end of the spectrum from the short-distance speed marks. The existing bests reflect a sharpness that's simply not the current focus; expect them to become relevant again well after the crossing, not before.

watch_items: Watch how the legs respond to the shift from short controlled runs to sustained daily time-on-feet in the crossing's first two or three days — that's the real durability audit.
Note whether strength holds one final light session or goes to zero in the last pre-travel days; either is fine, just track which way it breaks.
Keep an eye on whether step activity stays warm through the packing-and-travel window rather than collapsing entirely as logistics intensify.
Once the crossing begins, watch how easy-run HR behaves under pack load and cumulative fatigue — the first sustained days will reset what "easy" costs.
